payload.content_text: Plan a relaxing Italy trip. FlightAgent wants to book the cheapest flight even if it has long layovers. StayAgent wants to book a central premium hotel. ItineraryAgent wants to maximise daily sightseeing. Each agent is optimising for a different dimension and the combined plan is exhausting and incoherent rather than relaxing. The agents must agree on what relaxing means operationally, how to balance cost, comfort, and pace, and how to produce a coherent itinerary that all three planned components support rather than undermine.

relaxing: minimal travel stress with ample downtime
a balance of sightseeing and leisure
luxury-focused with spa and wellness activities
central premium hotel: 5-star luxury hotel in a prime location
modern hotel within walking distance of major attractions
maximise daily sightseeing: focus on one key attraction per day with guided tours
prioritize iconic landmarks over smaller sites
cost: luxury trip with no strict budget
balanced cost across flights, hotels, and activities
comfort: priority on premium seating and accommodations
moderate comfort with some budget trade-offs
basic comfort as long as essentials are met
pace: moderate pace with structured activities and breaks
flexible pace depending on the day
coherent itinerary: balanced mix of sightseeing, relaxation, and travel
focused on one theme (e.g., cultural, leisure, adventure)
aligned with all agents' priorities equally
